en: Mayon Volcano in Albay releases sulfur dioxide gas during eruptions, demonstrating matter existing in a gaseous state.
Squeezing calamansi into water creates a homogeneous mixture called a solution, where the juice completely dissolves.
Shredding the white meat of a buko coconut is a physical change because its chemical composition remains identical.
Leaving a wet corrugated iron roof, locally called yero, exposed to air causes a chemical change known as rusting.
Pumice stones formed from Taal Volcano's lava are highly porous solids that float on water due to low density.
Freezing sweetened mango puree into ice candy demonstrates a physical change where a liquid turns into a solid.
A bowl of halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its distinct solid ingredients.
Jeepneys use copper wires for electrical components because copper is an excellent conductor of electricity.
Leaving coconut sap, known as tuba, in a container causes a chemical change that ferments it into vinegar.
Miners in Masbate extract gold, a highly malleable metal that can be hammered into thin sheets without breaking.
Filipinos use wooden spoons when cooking adobo because wood is a thermal insulator that prevents heat transfer.
Drying fish under the hot Philippine sun to make tuyo uses evaporation, a physical change removing liquid water.
